THE_DEFECT.symptom: The first run ever to call experiments/run_state.py::seal reached AUDIT_FAILED on a single gating check, seed_class: 'block 20200001..20200064 OVERLAPS 1 registered block(s): ROUTED_COMPOSITION_OUTCOME_V1 20200001..20200064 [sealed_confirmatory/RESERVED]'.
THE_DEFECT.diagnosis: The overlapping block WAS the run's own Rule-9 reservation. run_audit called seed_registry.check_block(lo, hi, seed_class) with no experiment_id, so the auditor had no way to know who owned the block and read the run's own record as foreign reuse.
THE_DEFECT.scope: Latent and general, not specific to this experiment. Rule 9 requires allocating the block BEFORE spending seeds, so by audit time every compliant run has its own reservation on record. Every Rule-9-abiding run would have failed its own seal the same way. Rules 7 and 9 were mutually unsatisfiable in practice until now.
THE_DEFECT.why_it_survived_until_now: Rules 7-9 were infrastructure only; docs/RESEARCH_RUN_STANDARDS.md recorded that no evaluator had yet been migrated onto seal(). The gate was proven by its tests rather than by use, and none of the 14 existing tests registered a block and then audited it under its own name.
THE_DEFECT.why_pre_launch_checking_did_not_catch_it: A synthetic dry-run of run_audit was executed before launch and passed, but at that moment the seed block had not yet been allocated, so no overlap existed. The contract stage's C11 called check_block WITH experiment_id and correctly passed. The defect lives only on the path where allocation has happened and the auditor is not told the owner -- a state that first exists after the outcome loop begins.
THE_DEFECT.severity_note: This is a false-negative on a bookkeeping check, the safe direction for an integrity gate to fail. It refused to seal a good record; it did not seal a bad one.

THE_FIX.change_1: AuditPlan gains an optional field experiment_id: str | None = None -- the registry owner of the seed block.
THE_FIX.change_2: The seed_class check now calls check_block(min(want), max(want), plan.seed_class, experiment_id=plan.experiment_id) and records the owner in the check data.
THE_FIX.no_change_needed_in_seed_registry: experiments/seed_registry.py::check_block ALREADY implements the required semantics and already accepted an experiment_id. It auto-allows only an exact same-experiment, same-range match and routes everything else through the normal overlap check. Its source comments document a previously-fixed bug in exactly this area. Nothing in the registry was modified.
THE_FIX.why_this_cannot_become_a_bypass: Ownership is not a skip. A same-named request for a DIFFERENT range -- wider, shifted or partially overlapping -- falls through to the ordinary overlap check, so a run cannot silently expand its own allocation by re-auditing with a wider block instead of going through allocate(). Omitting experiment_id preserves the old strict behaviour exactly, so existing callers are unaffected.

REGRESSION_TESTS_ADDED.isolation: All five monkeypatch seed_registry.load onto a synthetic registry, so they never read or write artifacts/SEED_REGISTRY.json.

THE_VERDICT_DOES_NOT_DEPEND_ON_THIS_DEFE.statement: Even with the seed audit passing, the routed strategy fails the frozen scientific joint gate.

THE_VERDICT_DOES_NOT_DEPEND_ON_THIS_DEFE.no_retuning_follows_from_this: The operating point stays frozen. Retuning a threshold now, after seeing outcome numbers, is exactly the outcome-driven tuning the selector freezes were written to prevent.
